$schema: Each key is an event id from docs/design/events.md (plus quiet_day, illness.<condition-id>, and derelict_* outcome variants). Value: array of text variants. Placeholders: {name} crew member, {n} number, {item} supply name.
quiet_day: Nothing happened today. The crew found this suspicious.
The stars held still. So did everything else.
A quiet day. Somebody wrote it down in case it never happens again.
The drives hummed. Nobody complained, which was a first.
The crew played cards for rations they already owned.
Dull day aboard. The ship's cat, if there is one, was not consulted.
The coffee was bad in the usual way. Morale held.
Hours of empty space went by, as scheduled.
Someone counted the rations twice. The number did not improve.
The hull ticked and creaked, then thought better of it.
A buoy blinked in the distance and was not heard from again.
The crew debated whether it was Tuesday. It was not settled.
The ship's clock lost four minutes. It was returned.
The view was stars. They were the same stars as yesterday, mostly.
Somebody hummed a hymn through the whole afternoon shift.
The recycler gurgled once, with feeling, and went quiet.
The crew mended socks. In space this counts as a hobby.
Not a single alarm sounded. The captain checked the alarms.
The Lane stayed where it was. A small mercy.
A dull glow on the horizon turned out to be a dull glow.
Everyone agreed the day was fine. Nobody trusted it.
The ship drifted through nothing at a respectable pace.
A long, level watch. The log entry is one word: fine.
The captain read the manual again. It was no more helpful.
The hull sang something low and cheerful. The crew pretended not to hear.
A day so uneventful the logbook asked for a refund.
The crew drew straws for dishes. Everyone lost at once.
Someone waved at a passing buoy. The buoy said nothing, politely.
The drives held steady. The crew held a quiet grudge against the recycler.
Dinner was paste, and dessert was also paste.
The captain wrote 'no incidents' in the log and knocked on a bulkhead.
Nobody fell ill, died or got lost. The crew felt vaguely cheated.
The stars shifted a hair to the left. Or the ship did.
illness: {name} is not feeling well. The medical locker has opinions.
{name} took to a bunk with a look nobody liked.
{name} has come down with something. The manual calls it a condition.
illness.space-dysentery: {name} has caught space dysentery. The recycler is being blamed.
{name} has space dysentery. The bunks nearest the head have been reassigned.
{name} has space dysentery. Nobody is sure how, and nobody asked.
illness.hull-mold-fever: {name} has hull mold fever. The walls look smug about it.
{name} has hull mold fever. The mold has been asked to leave.
{name} has come down with hull mold fever and a green cough.
illness.cryo-fever: {name} has cryo-fever. They are cold, then colder, then confusing.
{name} has caught cryo-fever. Blankets have been requisitioned.
{name} has cryo-fever. The thermostat is innocent, officially.
illness.scurvy: {name} has scurvy. It is 2184 and the gums have not heard.
{name} has scurvy. The crew suggests fruit, of which there is none.
illness.radiation-sickness: {name} has radiation sickness. The suit was, regrettably, in the locker.
{name} has radiation sickness and a mild glow. This is not a joke.
{name} has radiation sickness. The manual said this would not happen.
illness.exhaustion: {name} is exhausted. The drives have been running longer than anyone.
{name} has fallen asleep on watch, upright. The crew is worn thin.
The crew is exhausted, {name} most of all. The ship, strangely, is not.
illness.decompression-injury: {name} has a decompression injury. It is mostly the bruise that talks.
{name} came through the crossing with a decompression injury and a story.
{name} has a decompression injury. They will tell it at every station.
illness.micrometeorite-puncture: {name} was punctured by a micrometeorite. The suit would have helped, had it been worn.
A micrometeorite pierced {name}. It was very small and very sure of itself.
{name} has a micrometeorite puncture. The pebble has not been found.
pirates: Pirates boarded while you slept. They took {n} {item} and left a note complimenting the coffee.
Pirates took {n} {item} and apologized for the inconvenience. The apology was on a form.
Raiders came aboard politely and left with {n} {item}. They signed the manifest.
Pirates relieved you of {n} {item}. They said it was nothing personal.
lost_lane: You lost the Lane. It took {n} days to find a buoy that would admit to being one.
The buoys went quiet and the ship went sideways. You lost {n} days finding the Lane.
You drifted off the Lane. The cost was {n} days and some dignity.
drive_failure: An ion drive has died. It made a small sound and then no more sound.
An ion drive has failed for good. The crew stood about with hats off, metaphorically.
One of your drives has given up. It had a long run and a bad attitude.
drive_stall: An ion drive has stalled. It needs {n} days of rest and a stern word.
A drive went offline for {n} days. Coaxing was attempted and ignored.
A drive sulked and shut itself down for {n} days. Nobody asked it why.
hull_puncture: A hull plate has cracked. The crew applied tape, which is not in the manual.
The hull took a hit and a plate gave out. It is, strictly, a leak.
A hull plate has broken. You can hear the cold from the corridor.
pump_failure: The coolant pump has failed. The ship will not move until it is mended.
The coolant pump coughed twice and stopped. The drives are waiting, politely.
The pump is broken. Everything else is fine, which is no help.
gyro_failure: The nav gyro has failed. North is now a matter of opinion.
The nav gyro is broken. It has been pointing at nothing for an hour.
The gyro gave out. The crew navigates by feel, and feel is not good.
hull_fire: A fire in the galley burned {n} rations. {name} was scorched putting it out.
Fire broke out aft. It cost {n} rations, and {name} came out singed.
A small fire became a large one. {n} rations burned, and {name} is sore.
crew_eva_drift: {name} went out on a spacewalk and drifted off. They should be back in {n} days.
{name} is adrift on a tether that is no longer tethered. Expect {n} days.
{name} stepped outside for air, of which there is none. Back in {n} days.
bad_recycler: The water recycler has gone bad. The crew drank before anyone noticed.
The recycler is running brown. Everyone is a little worse for it.
Bad water. The recycler is sorry, and so is everyone who drank it.
derelict: You came upon a derelict. It was empty, and it was clearly there first.
A dark hull drifted past. The crew searched it and found only dust and a calendar.
A wreck hung off the starboard side. It was already picked clean, by the look.
derelict_nothing: You searched a derelict and found nothing but a calendar from 2149.
The derelict had been picked clean. Someone had left a polite note saying so.
derelict_rations: You found a derelict with {n} rations still in the locker. Nobody asked who the previous owner was.
The wreck held {n} rations, mostly sealed. You took them without a speech.
derelict_part: A derelict gave up a spare: one {item}, in good order. The ship was grateful.
You salvaged a spare {item} from a drifting hulk. It was warm and strangely welcome.
derelict_suits: A derelict held {n} EVA suits, used but sealed. The crew is better dressed.
You found {n} suits in a wreck. They smell of someone else, which is acceptable.
algae_bloom: An algae bloom in the tank yielded {n} rations. It tastes like pond, but it is food.
The hydroponics bay bloomed overnight. You gained {n} rations and a green smell.
A wild algae bloom turned up in the tanks. {n} rations were harvested, thankfully.
belter_help: A passing Belter pointed to a cache and left. You gained {n} rations and thanked the dark.
Belters shared {n} rations and no conversation. It was a good trade.
A Belter tossed over {n} rations and a grunt. The grunt was friendly.
cargo_shift: The cargo shifted coming out of the crossing. {n} {item} went missing in the hold.
Loose lashing. You lost {n} {item} to the crossing and a bad knot.
The crossing shook the hold, and {n} {item} did not survive the shaking.
scan.nothing: The drones swept the wreckage and returned with a tin of regret.
Nothing worth hauling. The drones sound almost apologetic.
Three hours of scanning, one dented bolt. You leave the bolt.
The wreck was picked clean by someone with better drones.
scan.part: The drones hauled in a spare {item}, only slightly haunted.
A spare {item} was bobbing in the debris. The drones were thrilled.
Salvage report: one {item}, in working order, previous owner unknown.
scan.rations: The drones salvaged {n} rations. Nobody asked whose they were.
Good scan: {n} rations, sealed and mostly not expired.
The drones came back with {n} rations and a smug beep.
A cargo crate yielded {n} rations. The label was in a language of hope.
repair.success: You repaired the {item}. It sounds almost cheerful.
The {item} is fixed. The manual may take credit.
New part in, old part out. The {item} works again.
The {item} holds. You decline to ask why.
repair.fail: The repair failed. The {item} is still broken, but now it is also insulted.
No luck. The {item} remains broken, and you remain hopeful.
You tried. The {item} did not, so try again or pray.
The {item} refused the repair. It had its reasons.
repair.failLost: The repair failed and the spare {item} is ruined. A bad day for hardware.
You ruined the spare {item} and fixed nothing. A full set of losses.
The spare {item} did not survive your attempt. Neither did the repair.
help.part: A passing crew fixed your {item} and declined payment. They left a note.
Strangers in a patched tug repaired your {item} and drifted on.
A kind hauler lent a wrench and fixed the {item}. Lane manners still exist.
help.drive: A passing hauler spared you an ion drive. You owe them a story.
A convoy captain tossed you a spare drive. 'Pay it forward,' he said.
Strangers gave you an ion drive and refused thanks. Space is odd that way.
weather.calm: Calm skies. The ship hums, and nobody suspects a thing.
Calm today. Even the dust is lying low.
A quiet stretch of nothing. You make the most of it.
The void behaves. Enjoy it while it lasts.
weather.fair: Fair skies. The Lane lies open and the buoys blink along.
A fair day, by Lane standards, which is a low bar.
Fair weather. Radiation is within what the pamphlet promised.
Fair. The sensors are bored, and that is the best sign.
weather.unsettled: Unsettled skies. The sensors twitch at things that are not there.
Unsettled. The hull creaks a little, in the way hulls do.
Dust and static ahead. Nothing serious, probably.
The sky is unsettled. So is the crew, mildly.
weather.storm: Solar storm. Suits on, and no one makes jokes about sunbathing.
A solar storm rolls in. The hull ticks like an angry clock.
Storm warning: the sun is in a mood. Stay inside if you can.
Charged particles by the bucket. The suits earn their keep.
weather.fog: Ion fog. The buoys are rumors, and the compass is a suggestion.
Thick ion fog. You steer by faith and a blinking light.
Fog on the Lane. Every shadow turns out to be another shadow.
The ion fog slows you to a careful crawl.
weather.flare: Flare. Proxima is throwing a tantrum, and you are in the way.
A flare lights the sky. The shielding makes a worrying noise.
Flare overhead. Everyone finds a reason to be near the suits.
Proxima flares. The ship ticks and prays.
rejoin: {name} drifted back aboard, looking sheepish and slightly sunburned.
{name} climbed back through the airlock. The tether was, in fact, optional.
{name} is back aboard. Nobody mentions the drifting.
delay: A lost day. The ship holds position and the crew holds its breath.
The ship waits out the day, going nowhere in the most careful way.
Another day lost to drifting. The Lane is patient, and you are less so.
stuck: The ship cannot move today. It has run out of reasons to try.
No drives, no motion. The ship sits and thinks about it.
You are going nowhere. The silence is thorough.
starving: The crew is starving. The paste jokes have stopped.
Empty lockers, empty stomachs. The crew's patience thins.
Nobody has eaten, and everybody has noticed.
suit_wear: An EVA suit was ruined by the radiation. It will not be missed, but it will be needed.
Radiation chewed through a suit seam. One suit fewer between you and the sun.
A suit gave up the ghost today. The lining went first.
rest: The crew rests. Some even sleep, which is the point.
A day of rest. The ship drifts and the crew mends.
The crew takes a day off, as the manual allows once a month.
Rest day. Boots off, coffee on, hull still holding.
recover.space-dysentery: {name} has recovered from space dysentery. The recycler is still blamed.
{name} is over the space dysentery, and back on solid food.
The space dysentery has let {name} go. Nobody is sure why.
recover.hull-mold-fever: {name} has shaken off the hull mold fever. The walls are still suspected.
{name} is clear of hull mold fever, and sleeping away from the bulkhead.
The hull mold fever has passed. {name} is pale but opinionated.
recover.cryo-fever: {name} has recovered from the cryo-fever and is warm again.
The cryo-fever broke overnight. {name} asks for soup.
{name} is through the cryo-fever, a little thinner and a lot wiser.
recover.scurvy: {name} has recovered from scurvy. The algae finally did its job.
The scurvy has lifted. {name} can smile without wincing.
{name} is rid of the scurvy and has a new respect for greens.
recover.radiation-sickness: {name} has recovered from radiation sickness. The glow has faded.
{name} is past the radiation sickness, and holding the suit a little closer.
The radiation sickness is gone. {name} counts it as a lesson.
recover.exhaustion: {name} has recovered from exhaustion and asks for no more overburn.
{name} slept for ten hours straight. The exhaustion has lifted.
The exhaustion is gone. {name} has opinions about thrust settings.
recover.decompression-injury: {name} has recovered from the decompression injury. The bones knit and the pride too.
{name} is healed of the decompression injury, and checks every seal twice.
The decompression injury is mended. {name} still avoids the airlock.
recover.micrometeorite-puncture: {name} has recovered from the micrometeorite puncture. A scar remains for stories.
The micrometeorite puncture has closed. {name} counts it a lucky hole.
{name} is over the micrometeorite puncture and wants a bigger suit.
salvage.haul: The drone towed in {n} rations and {parts}. It looks pleased with itself.
Salvage run: {n} rations and {parts}, all of it dented and all of it yours.
The drone came home with {n} rations and {parts}. Nobody asked where it learned to steal.
salvage.haulRations: The drone towed in {n} rations. It hovered by the hatch, waiting to be told it was good.
Salvage run: {n} rations, slightly used. The drone has no regrets.
salvage.haulParts: The drone towed in {parts} and no rations. Mechanics were thrilled; cooks were not.
Salvage run: {parts}. The pantry was not consulted.
salvage.nothing: The drone came back with scrap and a bent grapple. It would rather not discuss it.
Nothing worth towing. The drone blames the debris, the light, and you.
A day of grappling, a hold full of nothing. The drone sulks in its cradle.
salvage.wrecked: The drone was wrecked out there. It limped home with half of what it had hooked.
Too many dents. The drone gave up and towed in only half its haul.
The drone took its third hit and went dark. A tug brought back half the haul.
salvage.hot: {name} unloaded a glowing chunk bare-handed. It was warm and not food.
The hold smelled of ozone. {name} says that is probably fine.
salvage.overweight: You could only tow 100 units back. {n} rations drift off toward Neptune.
The tow cable held at 100 units. {n} rations went on without you, toward Neptune.
Over the carry limit. {n} rations were left behind to be somebody else's lucky day.
threading.clean: Clean thread. Not one rock touched the hull, and the hull looks relieved.
You threaded the gap without a scratch. The rocks seemed embarrassed.
threading.hit: Rock strikes: {hits}. The hull has opinions.
Hull strikes logged: {hits}. The rocks kept score.
{hits} rock strikes. The paint has seen better days.
flare.clean: Rode the wind. Not one arc touched you, and the crew has stopped holding its breath.
A clean ride through the flares. The ship hums like it meant to.
flare.scorch: A flare cooked the hold. {n} {item} came out looking toasted.
Scorched cargo: {n} {item} are now a lesson in packing.
The flare licked the hold and {n} {item} were ruined.
flare.burn: A flare flashed across the deck. {name} has a burn and a new respect for shade.
{name} caught the edge of an arc. It was a short, bright, unwelcome moment.
{name} was singed by a flare and is taking it personally.
flare.damage: A flare hit the ship and your {item} is broken.
The plasma found a weak spot. Your {item} is broken.
An arc crossed the hull and left your {item} in pieces.
flare.radiation: A flare soaked {name} in radiation. The sickness comes later, like the bill.
{name} was caught unsuited in the arc. Sickness has been scheduled.
The flare passed through {name} without asking. The doctor will ask for them.
flare.crash: Five hits. The Flare Belt took {name} and half the hold, and left you the hull.
The ship ran out of luck and flare-free sky. {name} did not come back from it.
The wind threw you off. {name} is gone, and the cargo is half of what it was.
info.skipped: The run was abandoned and the crew settled it the sensible way. It cost extra.
You called it off. The statistical route was shorter and worse.
